title: Loaded Potato Feed
subtitle: Self-serve spuds for twenty
description: Self-serve spuds for twenty. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Loaded Potato Feed in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Stage two oven racks
steps.instruction: Heat two ovens (or rotate batches) to 400°F. Scrub and poke all russets; oil and salt the skins. For twenty-plus eaters, bake in waves on sheet pans if rack space is tight.

steps.title: Bake potatoes in batches
steps.instruction: Bake 50–65 minutes until fork-tender. Transfer finished potatoes to foil-lined cambros at 200°F while the next batch bakes. Never cover hot potatoes tightly — steam softens skins.

steps.title: Set a long topping line
steps.instruction: Arrange butter, cheddar, bacon, sour cream, green onions, and warm pulled beef in a row with labels. Put a trash can and extra forks at the end — this feed gets messy in the best way.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Loaded Potato Feed onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve family-style
steps.instruction: Call the crew when the first cambro is full. Split potatoes at the line; let everyone build their own loaded spud. Refill toppings before the pan looks empty — empty cheddar bowls cause hall riots.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Loaded Potato Feed — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Firefighters eat heavy after rough nights — double the protein if the hall had a busy shift.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Label every topping bowl — rookies grab faster when they can read the line.
Keep hot bases (potatoes, chips) in cambros at 200°F and cold toppings on ice if service runs long.
Put forks, napkins, and a trash can at the end of the bar — self-serve feeds get messy fast.
Serve family-style from two full-size trays — never let the line run dry on a busy night.
Put starch and protein on separate trays so vegetarians can load up on sides.
Line up Loaded Potato Feed on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Self-serve spuds for twenty. A hall pick for big-appetite nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Loaded Potato Feed runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
